title: Drug Resistance Is Heading Toward A Cancer-Sized Death Toll
hook: Routine infections are learning to outlast the medicines built to stop them.
closing: Preserving effective antibiotics protects ordinary medical care from becoming far more dangerous.
question: Can medicine stay ahead of resistance?

segments.say: Drug resistance directly killed 1.27 million people in 2019. Routine infections already carry a major global toll.
Drug resistance deaths could reach 10 million yearly by 2050. Today's toll is only the beginning of the projected rise.
Projected resistance deaths equal 10 million current cancer deaths yearly. The future toll would be cancer-sized.
